notes: PLACEMENT FAILURES (not placed, within budget): Lynas USA Seadrift TX: Mining Weekly and Northern Miner returned 403 / TLS errors; Kitco (opened, 2025-08-28, https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2025-08-28/lynas-flags-uncertainty-over-texas-rare-earths-plant-posts-profit) quotes 'warned of considerable uncertainty over the future of its heavy rare earths processing plant in Texas' and 'construction of the plant may not move forward', but does not name Seadrift. Search summaries (unopened) say Seadrift, a 2025 DoD offtake negotiation, a $258M expenditure-based DoD funding figure, and a 2,500-3,000 t/yr heavy REE target; none could be quoted. No 2026 status found.

PLACEMENT FAILURES: Energy Fuels heavy REE plant: a 10-Q (search summary only, unopened) says construction of a commercial-scale heavy rare earth plant at the Mill was announced 2026-07-29. A Bloomberg 2026-03-25 item (unopened) reports first terbium oxide. The FY2025 10-K (opened, first 100k chars) says the mill is in 'Utah' and describes 'work on our planned continued development of capabilities for the commercial separation of REEs at our White Mesa Mill' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1385849/000138584926000009/efr-20251231.htm). Monazite throughput from FY2025 is unquoted. Current status should be confirmed against the 10-Q.

Energy Fuels row: the FY2020 10-K is used for the city and state. The product field's rare earth text is supported by the FY2025 10-K, not by the FY2020 quote. Published date is not shown on the opened page (null).

Westwater Kellyton: status 'announced' reflects only the opened 2021 release. Unopened search summaries (FY2025 10-K; BusinessWire 2022 groundbreaking, 403) say the plant is under construction for more than three years, on about 70 acres under a Lake Martin Area IDA lease in Coosa County, with a targeted 2023 operation date and a $202 million groundbreaking figure. Those should be quoted in a later pass. The opened 2021 release says 'initial investment of $80 million or more' (not quoted in-row because the row quote supports the city). Phase I capacity of about 16,000 mt/yr is from the unopened FY2022 10-K.

Noveon San Marcos: the opened grand-opening article (June 2023) says '150,000+ square foot headquarters'; other unopened pages give 145,000 and 132,000 sq ft. Only the opened figure is reported here, and acres are null. Unopened search summaries cite a $215M domestic expansion centered on San Marcos (date and details unconfirmed) and 10,000-ton long-term output. Local tax terms (Chapter 380/381, 10-year rebates) are in unopened search summaries only. The 100-job figure is '100+' on the page.

Gallium: the pulse2 article (2026-08-29) says ATALCO 'constructed a pilot primary gallium production facility at Gramercy' and that the total is $800 million in public and private funding during 2026, including $350M of preferred equity (unopened summary). Status is 'announced' because the commercial circuit is not yet operating. Other US gallium activity, unopened: ElementUSA red-mud demonstration at Gramercy (Metallium technology) and Alcoa exploration at Saline County AR. Alcoa's gallium plant is in Western Australia, which is outside scope.

Copper: the Aurubis 2021 release is the opened source. Its investment ($340 million / EUR 300 million) and 125 jobs are in the release. The row keeps the location quote, so investment is in the notes. Unopened search summaries report a September 2024 ribbon cutting and a September 2025 production start, which would make the status 'operating'. Verify before publishing. Freeport-McMoRan Miami AZ: no opened page gave the Miami, Arizona location in a quotable sentence. Search results were the FY2025 Annual Report (PDF, not opened) and job postings. Not placed. Rio Tinto Kennecott (Magna UT) was not searched within budget.

Manganese: Element 25 Ascension Parish (opened Opportunity Louisiana release, 2023-04-12) says 'exploring plans to invest $480 million across two phases' and 'high-purity manganese sulfate monohydrate production facility in Ascension Parish'. The city is not on any opened page (Burnside appears only in an unopened search summary), so no facility row was written. nacleanenergy (403) would have given the site. Search summaries also give a 35-acre site, a GM offtake of up to 32,500 t/yr and a $57.1M state incentive, none opened. South32 Hermosa: the opened Northern Miner article (2024-09-20) says the processing facility 'location is yet to be determined, it will be in southern Arizona' and gives $166M DOE funding without naming a program. The mine is in the Patagonia Mountains. No processing-plant city, so not placed.

Lithium: Standard Lithium / Equinor South West Arkansas (opened release, 2025-01-16) says 'located in Lafayette and Columbia Counties, Arkansas', closes a '$225 million grant from the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Manufacturing & Energy Supply Chains', and expects '45,000 tonnes per annum of lithium carbonate'. No city on the opened page, so no facility row. El Dorado AR is the demonstration plant per an unopened summary. The NEPA Environmental Assessment condition and the 2025 FID target are unopened search summaries. Exxon Mobil Arkansas, Piedmont Kings Mountain hydroxide, and Century Lithium were not searched within budget.

Graphite: Anovion Bainbridge: the opened Manufacturing Dive article (2023-05-22) says '$800 million in a manufacturing facility in Bainbridge, Georgia', 'over 400 jobs', '40,000 metric tons of synthetic graphite annually', and 'received $117 million from the Department of Energy last year under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law'. The doe_award field is null because the row quote supports location and investment. Treat the DOE award as supported by that same opened page (quote above). Status after 2023 is not confirmed; an unopened summary says construction started in late 2024 and completion was expected late 2025. Urbix was not searched within budget.

Perpetua Resources / Army / INL antimony trisulfide pilot: opened East Idaho News (2026-07-30) says 'with the commissioning of a new modular mineral processing plant at the Idaho National Laboratory' and 'approximately one ton of ore per day'. The opened page does not name Idaho Falls or Idaho, so no facility row. Unopened sources say the ribbon cutting was 2026-07-29 in Idaho Falls, Perpetua received up to $15.5M in DoD funding, and federal and Army awards since 2022 total over $87M. The US Forest Service Final Record of Decision for Stibnite (2025-01-03) is unopened. The EXIM financing figures conflict ($1.8B vs $2.7B) and are not reported.
Citation-quality caveat: WebFetch returns model-processed extracts, not raw HTML. Quotes above are the strings it returned in quotation marks. Confirm each against the live page before publishing.

Tool budget: about 35 calls. Not searched within budget: Rio Tinto Kennecott, Exxon Mobil Arkansas, Piedmont Kings Mountain, Century Lithium, Urbix, Lynas for a second source. Gallium coverage is one facility only.
